message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • General limit: 55 mph on rural roads, 45 mph on urban roads.
• 70 mph on interstate highways (except where posted otherwise).
• 65 mph on rural two‑lane highways. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Regulations | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• No “seat‑belt law” for drivers over 18, but all passengers must buckle. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is prohibited (unless using a hands‑free system).
• Texting while driving is illegal. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (0.02% BAC).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• “Move‑over” law: vehicles must change lanes or slow down when approaching emergency vehicles. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Headlights & Lighting** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise, and during any weather that reduces visibility.
• Fog lights may only be used when visibility is less than 200 ft. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display valid registration stickers.
• Towing regulations require proper permits and safety chains. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **School Bus Rules** | • All vehicles must stop for a school bus with its stop sign extended and lights flashing. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Parking & Loading Zones** | • No parking within 20 ft of a crosswalk or intersection.
• Parking in a loading zone requires a permit. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Traffic Cameras & Automated Enforcement** | • Cameras enforce speed limits, red‑light violations, and other infractions. | TxDOT Automated Enforcement Program | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Bicyclists must ride in the lane if one exists; otherwise, they may ride on the shoulder.
• Motorcycles must use the right side of the lane. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Penalties & Fines** | • Fines vary by offense; DUI can lead to up to 2 years in jail.
• Points added to driver’s record can lead to license suspension. | Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) – Penalties & Points | ### How to Get Official, Up‑to‑Date Information 1. **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – [DPS Traffic Laws](https://www.dps.texas.gov/section/driver-licensing/traffic-laws) 2. **Texas Transportation Code** – Available online via the Texas Legislature’s website. 3. **TxDOT** – For road‑specific regulations and speed limits. 4. **Local County Courts** – For specific citations or legal questions. --- #### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s the single most effective way to reduce injury. - **Avoid distractions** – put your phone on “Do Not Disturb” while driving. - **Observe speed limits** – they’re posted for a reason; exceeding them can lead to hefty fines. - **Be mindful of school buses** – stopping is mandatory; failure can result in a 30‑day license suspension. - **Check your vehicle’s registration** – expired stickers can lead to a ticket even if you’re not speeding. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law or how to handle a particular traffic situation!
